chapter: Early years in Brenham and Houston
title: Recording discs in the early days and making first records
summary: The interviewer describes the red-light acoustic disc recording process; Harris recalls saving the shavings from his first records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: It's alright when the red light go on. Go ahead. When the red light would go on then you start to recording. Now the man in the back that's recording it, there was a little light thread would come off of that disc and it would pile up and then you'd have to wrap it up and take it off and throw it on the floor. And that was one continuous operation until you cut the disc and then the lights would go on and nobody said a word, nothing dropped on the floor, you couldn't breathe too hard. That's right. Today it's a lot different.
That's the way it was now we made our first records. We were so crazy about the records we even saved that little, that little shave in it. And I kept that for a long time.
Look at that I made records, you don't believe it?
